_about: The steps of a walk-in's visit (see CustomerManager): waiting at the host stand, being led to a table, the drink order, the drink, the food order, eating, the bill. Townsfolk say one of these lines at each step ({drink}, {dish} fill in). Regulars use their own lines from their character file instead (events seating, drink_order, drink_served, served, farewell). Townsfolk say the drink order, food order, food arriving and the bill in a dialogue box, the rest in a speech bubble. regular_stay_seconds: a regular who hasn't been chatted with stays this long after their food arrives before asking for the bill, saying a get_going line get_going_warning_seconds before. delivery_question: what a townsfolk asks at the bill once the restaurant has been open delivery_question_day days, which puts a phone on the wall the next morning; phone_installed is the news that morning.
delivery_question: Do you deliver? I'd order every night if you did.
phone_installed: A phone was put up on the wall last night. Customers can call in delivery orders now, and once the dinner rush is over, the night shift takes calls.
_townsfolk: What townsfolk (not regulars) say at each step, one picked at random. served_<tier> fits how the dish came out (perfect, great, okay, burnt), falling back to served; eating is their bubble while they eat, by the same tiers.

drink_order: I'll have a {drink} while I look.
served_perfect: Wow, look at that! It's perfect!
This looks too good to eat!
served_burnt: Is it... supposed to be this dark?
wrong_drink: Oh, that's not what I asked for... it's fine.
bill: I'm all done. The bill, please!

regular_get_going: I should get going soon. Just finishing up.
_guide: The Guide's arrow for new chefs: one per player, pointing the walking way to their next step, with a line at the bottom of their view (hints, by step; {name}, {verb}, {station} and {dish} are filled in). Shown to a new chef (until they've finished their first customer, or worked a shift), or to everyone with the Guide arrow setting. A new chef's first customer is followed through the whole visit (the wait_ hints show, with no arrow, while there's nothing to do for them), then a box in their view says lesson_done_title and lesson_done, with a chime, until they press on, and the arrow's gone for them from then on.

guide.lesson_done: Now on to the rest of the customers! You know the way now, so you're on your own from here.

hints.open_up: Open up for the day at the host stand
hints.seat: A customer is waiting: seat them at the host stand
hints.make_drink: Make the drink at the drinks counter
hints.give_drink: Bring the drink to the customer who ordered it
hints.clip: Clip the ticket on the ticket wheel
hints.freezer: Get the ingredients from the freezer
hints.pick_up: Pick up what's waiting on the pass
hints.bag: Bag it to go at the takeout counter
hints.courier: Hand the bag to the courier
hints.print_bill: A customer wants the bill: print it at the host stand
hints.give_bill: Give the bill to the customer
hints.take_bin: Take a dish bin from the sink
hints.clear: Clear the dirty table into the bin
hints.wash: Wash the dishes at the sink
hints.bin_back: Put the bin back at the sink
hints.ring_bell: Everyone's served: ring the bell at the host stand
hints.wait_eating: {name} is eating. They'll ask for the bill when they're done

_takeout: The takeout counter (TakeoutCounter): a cooked dish has to be bagged here before the courier takes it, or before it can be given as a gift. After hours, free hands can also pack something from the pantry, or order a dish to go (its ticket goes in your pocket, and it's cooked the usual way). A bag can be unpacked again. per_page: choices shown at once.

takeout.nothing: (The pantry's empty, and the kitchen's closed for orders. Try cooking something to go.)

_secrets: Things a regular hides in the chair they sat in, when they say a line with "hides" (CustomerManager, Seat). Once it's hidden, a glint shows on that chair; a chef with free hands can look and find it, for the reward in money. prompt is what the chair says, found the message ({chef} fills in).

lucky_coin.found: {chef} found something wedged into the chair: Cheddar's lucky coin! (+$10)
